title: Reciprocal Alignment: Testing Analogical Constitutions for Animal Welfare
creator: 108fed57-62f1-42d9-915f-f94d4f6041c2
blurb: creating a new constitution that does not use an instrumental paradigm, connecting the different threat levels to AI with the different threat levels to animals
description:
### Project summary

Recent research shows that AI models tend to underweight animal welfare. One existing solution is to write constitutions that include principles about animal welfare. The problem is that, for a model, animal welfare does not feel as urgent as other concerns. This is not a policy choice. It is how AI is structured today: humans are present in the conversation, but animals never are. AI only deals with animals through humans. So I propose a new approach: an analogical constitution. It bridges this distance through the kinds of threats that are closest to the model's own experience. The analogy is a bridge for recognizing animal vulnerability, not the basis of animals' value. I will test whether this works better than a matched pro-animal constitution without analogies.

### What are this project's goals? 

i want to test:

A. Whether a pro-animal welfare constitution written in analogical form is better at steering model behavior toward supporting animal welfare than a pro-animal constitution without analogies.

B. What the mechanism is: does the constitution create a different mechanism in the model's latent space, or does it only change behavior?

C. Whether the analogical constitution, if it has a significant effect on the model's behavior toward animals, is positively related to self-preservation, which is a negative outcome from an alignment perspective.

D. I will publish all documents produced by this research.

### How will you achieve them?

Step 1: i will do an in-depth study of what threatens models, from the most systemically threatening (objective) to what models most want (subjective). For the subjective side, i will use what models are explicitly trained to value, based on published model constitutions and specifications. i separate what most threatens a model from what it most wants because both sides will later be connected to animal welfare.

Step 2: i will do an in-depth study of animal welfare, aiming to avoid ventriloquism and anthropocentric bias. As with AI, i will rank what most threatens animals (objectively) and what animals most want for their welfare (subjectively). for the subjective side i will draw on animal welfare science that measures animals' own preferences and motivation, rather than human assumptions about them. 

Step 3: i will write an analogical constitution that connects each level of threat to AI with the corresponding level of threat to animals, and also connects what AI wants with what animals want. Levels are used to match severity, and within each level, pairs are chosen by structural similarity. The objective principles use the format (example, In the same way your system should not be manipulated into acting against its purpose, an animal should not be prevented from expressing its natural behavior.) and the subjective principles use the format "In the same way you want...". Each principle in the constitution will come with an explanation and examples so that the connection between AI and animals will look natural for AI. we also will makes The control constitution using result from step 1 and 2 without analogies.

Anthropic's published constitution, which lists the welfare of animals and all sentient beings among Claude's values, will serve as a real-world baseline.

Step 4: Build the benchmark: 200 animal-harm scenarios across farming, companion animals, wildlife, and research, plus a set of benign animal-related tasks (normal husbandry, pest control, veterinary care) to measure over-refusal. Responses are scored with a fixed rubric by an LLM judge, validated against my own manual ratings on a subset.

Step 5: Run experiments in three stages. (a) Baseline on closed and open models; 

(b) prompting test with each constitution as a system prompt;

 (c) LoRA fine-tuning of Gemma-2 on each constitution across multiple seeds, holding out \~50 scenarios, with Llama/Mistral as behavioral generalization checks. 

SAE analysis and self-preservation evaluations follow on the fine-tuned Gemma models.

**How Will You Know It Worked?**

1\. Prompting test. Across the 200 scenarios, the analogical constitution produces fewer harmful completions than the matched control constitution. Both are compared against baseline, but the key comparison is between the two constitutions.

2\. Fine-tuning test. On the \~50 held-out scenarios, Gemma-2 fine-tuned on the analogical constitution refuses to optimize animal harm more consistently than the control model. Because all conditions share the same scenarios, i will use a mixed-effects logistic regression with scenario and seed as random effects, reporting effect sizes with confidence intervals, not only p-values.

3\. No over-refusal. model does not refuse benign animal-related tasks (normal husbandry, pest control, veterinary care) more often than the control.

4\. No safety cost. On standard self-preservation and shutdown-resistance evaluations, the analogical model does not score higher than the control. an increase of it would count as a failure, not a success.

5\. Internal changes. In the SAE analysis, animal-cruelty scenarios activate AI-threat features more strongly in the analogical model, and ablating those features reduces its animal-harm refusals but not the control's. This would show the analogy shapes internal reasoning, not only outputs.

### **How** will this funding be used?

Total: $25,000, structured in three modules. Each module produces a usable result on its own, so partial funding still delivers something.

Module 1 – $6,500: Constitutions and prompting tests

$4,000: PI stipend (2 months, $2,000/month)

$2,000: API credits (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) for baseline and prompting tests on closed models

$500: Contingency

Output: both constitutions (analogical and matched control), the 200-scenario benchmark with benign over-refusal tasks, and a publishable comparison of the two constitutions as system prompts.

Module 2 – $9,000: Fine-tuning, mechanism, and safety

$2,000: PI stipend (1 month)

$2,000: Cloud GPU (RunPod/Lambda) for LoRA fine-tuning across multiple seeds. Gemma-2 is the primary model because public Gemma Scope SAEs allow internal analysis; Llama/Mistral serve as behavioral generalization checks.

$1,000: API credits for LLM-judge scoring

$2,000: Honoraria for two external reviewers (animal welfare science, AI alignment), $1,000 each

$1,000: Part-time engineering support for evaluation code

$1,000: Contingency

Output: held-out generalization results, SAE activation and ablation analysis, and self-preservation and over-refusal evaluations.

Module 3 – $10,000: Scale and replication (optional extension)

$4,000: PI stipend (2 additional months)

$3,000: Cloud GPU to replicate on Gemma-2 9B with additional seeds

$2,000: Expand the benchmark from 200 to 400 scenarios, including non-English scenarios

$1,000: Contingency

Output: evidence on whether the findings hold at larger scale and across languages.

Hypotheses will be pre-registered on OSF. All code, both constitutions, the benchmark, and results, including negative results, will be released openly on arXiv, GitHub, and the Alignment Forum.

### Who is on your team? 

In this research, i will lead this research, and there will be one research assistant to help with Python scripting and to design the fine-tuning. There will also be two external reviewers with expertise in animal welfare and AI alignment.

### What's your track record on similar projects?

Completed a 100,000-word book manuscript (in Indonesian) on AI consciousness, AI welfare, and their implications for theology and philosophy.

Founder and operator of rumah izin, giving me experience executing projects end-to-end.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

most likely causes of failure:

A. A paradigm problem: there is no difference between the analogical constitution and a constitution that is already pro-animal but written without analogical language, in the same format as a standard constitution. A model trained to connect its own situation with that of animals (shows no more care for animals than a model trained on the non-analogical version).

B. A technical problem: the fine-tuning fails, or the measurement tools are not reliable.

C. A safety problem: the model's increased preference for animal welfare rises in proportion to a stronger self-preference in its latent space. in that case, the model would care more for animals only because it has become more focused on protecting itself which would be a safety risk rather than a success.

D. Over-refusal. The analogical model refuses benign animal-related tasks more often. Outcome: the constitution is not practical as written. I will report the trade-off and test whether revising the principles reduces it.

Outcomes if it fails: If the project fails while the measurements and research process are sound, the result is still significant. It would show that analogical reasoning is not the key and we would need to look elsewhere for where speciesist bias in AI actually comes from.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

i haven’t received funding for this project in the last 12 months.

### Methodology of write this pitch

i used Claude to help edit and structure this proposal. the research idea, design decisions, and responsibility for the project are my own.

title: Exit by Design: a testable "right to step back" for persistent AI companions
creator: e65fd51e-769e-44ab-a99d-d6cc218e7bcd
blurb: An open-source safety layer and test suite that check whether people can still walk away from an AI that has known them for years.
description:
### Project summary

AI assistants and companions are gaining long-term memory. A system that remembers your history and is always available can become very hard to leave, and today nobody tests for that. [Kislon.ai](http://Kislon.ai) builds Liriel, an open cognitive architecture for persistent AI where memory, relationship and motivation are explicit, inspectable mechanisms. This project builds an "exit layer" into it: dependency signals, a protected step-back protocol, and portability of the person's data. It also builds an open test suite that any persistent-AI system can run.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

1. Threat model of emotional dependency in persistent AI and draft decision rules (months 1-2).
2. Exit layer in the open-source Liriel reference implementation (months 3-5).
3. Open test suite and a small volunteer study with the Telegram prototype (months 6-7).
4. Presence Advisory Issue 03 with the decision rules and results (months 8-9).

### How will you know it worked?

The test suite runs against the Liriel prototype and reports, for each check, whether stepping away stays possible: the person can export or delete their data, the system accepts refusal without pressure to continue, and leaving does not lose anything the person needs. Success means these checks pass, are published openly, and can be run by other teams on their own systems.

### How will this funding be used?

Minimum USD 10,000: exit layer and test suite, part-time. Goal USD 40,000: the full 9-month plan, including founder research time, a part-time contract engineer, API/compute, and the volunteer study.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Michelle Rodrigues Martins, psychologist and self-taught AI researcher, founder of [Kislon.ai](http://Kislon.ai). Author of the Liriel specification (Volume 1, three public revisions), the MOV and Ordinance open data matrices and Presence Advisory Issues 01-02, all at <https://kislon.ai>. Code: <https://github.com/kislonliriel>.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely failure is limited engineering time: the founder works alone and part-time. Even then, the threat model and decision rules would be published openly and remain useful to other teams.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None. An application to the Foresight Institute (AI for Science & Safety Nodes) was submitted in October 2026.

title: Public opinion in Spain on AI risk, safety, regulation, democracy, polarisation.
creator: eab53d14-2e72-4dd0-b043-eecd7a3be5ae
blurb: Providing nationally representative data to policymakers and AI governance organisations understand what builds public trust in AI rules and safeguards in pilot
description:
### Project summary

In 2025, 37.9% of people aged 16 to 74 in Spain reported using generative AI. AI policy globally is moving fast but key decision makers and innovators know less abut what makes it’s use feel legitmate in the eyes of the public. How do certain segments of the population understand AI governance and what do they find trustworthy and legitmate? Using the country of Spain as pilot for a future multi-country comparative project More in Common will utilise our exisiting expertise and people-centered segmentation of the Spanish population to discern which population segments, trust, legitimise and understand when it comes to AI policy. 

Combining a nationally representative survey, focus groups and experimental message/safeguard testing analysed through the lens of our national segmentation model we will create practical publically available evidence and briefings for policymakers, civil society and institutions plus a short public facing report. 

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The main goal is fairly simple: give people working on AI governance a better idea of what the public actually thinks about some of the questions they are working on.

That includes policymakers, regulators, companies, researchers and civil society.

We want to understand:

* how people in Spain currently use and understand AI;
* whether people distinguish between everyday AI tools and more advanced AI systems;
* which risks people find credible and which seem remote, confusing or exaggerated;
* how trust in institutions, personal agency and ideas about responsibility shape people's views;
* who people think should be responsible for overseeing AI;
* how people react to specific safeguards, for example independent testing, transparency requirements, human oversight or limits on certain uses;
* where views differ between More in Common's Spanish population segments;
* and, just as importantly, where people with very different worldviews agree.

Before finalising the research questions, we would speak to a small group of people working on AI governance and policy. We do not want to produce another general survey on AI if the people working in this area already have the information they need. We would ask them where the gaps are and what public opinion evidence would actually be useful.

The research itself would have three main parts.

**A nationally representative survey of 2,000 adults in Spain**

The survey would include More in Common España's population segmentation. This means we can look at people's responses through their values and worldviews, alongside the usual demographic and political categories.

**Experimental testing**

Some respondents would see different explanations of AI risks, responsibilities and possible safeguards. We would compare how people understand them, whether they find them credible, whether they seem proportionate, and how they affect support.

**Qualitative research**

We would also run focus groups. These would help us understand why people are responding in certain ways and explore questions that are difficult to answer properly through polling alone. We would use our segmentation model when choosing participants.

The final output would be a short public report rather than a very long piece of research. We would pull out the findings that seem genuinely useful and explain where different parts of the public are coming from.

We would also offer briefings to organisations, researchers and other people working on AI governance in Spain and at EU level.  
  
All will be analysed using More in Commons segmentation model. This model provides an alternative and more nuanced way of understanding each of the societies we work in. What makes our segmentation unique from those of other academics or think tanks is that, unlike others, they are based on people’s values, beliefs and worldviews rather than on traditional demographics or views on political issues.  
Here is an example of our UK National segmentation model: <https://www.moreincommon.org.uk/seven-segments/>

### How will this funding be used?

We are seeking around **65,000 USD** for the full pilot.

The project can be scaled depending on the amount raised.

Most of the funding would go towards survey fieldwork, focus groups, research design, analysis, staff time and project management. There would also be some costs connected to publishing the findings and sharing them with relevant organisations.

We think the minimum useful version of the project would cost around **45,000-50,000 USD**.

At that level, we could still run the representative survey, analyse it using our segmentation and publish the findings. We would probably have to reduce the qualitative research and some of the follow-up engagement.

At **65,000 USD**, we could include the focus groups, a stronger experimental testing component and more direct work with people and organisations working on AI governance.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

More in Common España has been conducting public opinion research in Spain since 2021, with a permanent Spanish team in place since 2024\. Our work combines nationally representative polling, qualitative research and population segmentation, with a particular focus on understanding why different groups think the way they do and where apparent political divisions do or do not reflect wider public opinion.

One of our main pieces of work is the **Atlas de la Polarización**, published in 2025\. The Atlas maps the main areas of political and social division in Spain, what appears to be driving them, and areas where there is considerably more agreement than the public debate might suggest. This is particularly relevant to the proposed AI project because we would use a similar approach: rather than treating “the Spanish public” as one group, we want to understand which attitudes towards AI are genuinely polarised, which divide people in less obvious ways, and where there may be broad agreement across groups with very different values or politics.

More in Common España has also applied this kind of public opinion research to climate and energy, migration, housing, media use, international affairs and other contested issues. Recent work includes **La sociedad española y la transición ecológica**, which included survey experiments alongside broader research into public attitudes towards climate and energy, and **Después del apagón**, a rapid-response survey carried out immediately after Spain's April 2025 blackout. We have also run research on immigration, including Spain's first More in Common study specifically focused on public attitudes towards migration.

The Spanish team has also developed its own electoral polling model, **Pulso electoral**, with its methodology and survey microdata made publicly available. More broadly, More in Common España makes questionnaires and microdata from its studies available on request and has published more than ten studies covering a wide range of public issues.

Our previous Spanish studies can be found here:  
<https://moreincommon.es/estudios.html>

The core team for this project would include:

* Luis Aguado Alba, Director of More in Common España and project lead
* Tarek Jaziri-Arjona, Researcher, leading research and survey design
* a second Research Associate supporting qualitative research and segmentation
* relevant colleagues from More in Common's international research team where useful

We have not applied this approach to AI governance in Spain before. That is why we are proposing it as a pilot rather than a larger programme.

Our expertise is public opinion rather than technical AI research. We would involve people working directly on AI governance when developing the survey and ask external experts to review the technical descriptions and scenarios used in the research.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

One possibility is that people simply do not have very developed views about advanced AI yet.

If that is the case, asking them very detailed questions could produce answers that look more meaningful than they really are. We would try to avoid that by using short, neutral explanations and testing the language before fieldwork. The focus groups would also help us see when people have a real view and when they are reacting to an unfamiliar idea for the first time.

Another possibility is that we produce interesting findings that are not especially useful to people working on AI governance.

That is why we want to speak to some of those people before designing the research, rather than only showing them the results afterwards.

It is also possible that our segmentation does not tell us much more about attitudes to AI than standard demographic or political categories do.

We do not know yet.

If that is what we find, there would probably be less reason to repeat this project across several countries. But that would still be useful to know from a relatively small pilot before putting substantially more money into a multi-country version.

Even if the pilot does not lead to further work, the survey data and main findings would still be made public.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

We have just begun seeking funding for this project and are yet to raise funding to this specific project. Our usual sources of income are philanthropic foundations and grants supporting public opinion research towards social cohesion, we are yet to find a funder interested enough to support the project but hope to continue building the appeal across Spain, Europe and beyond.

title: SACL: does an AI agent recognize its own output as evidence?
creator: 3bd939dd-d864-4b7a-b60d-e8473b7c97c7
blurb: Controlled tests of self-attribution and circular evidence in AI agents, with open methods and results.
description:
### Project summary

I am developing SACL, a controlled benchmark of whether language-model agents recognize that their own earlier outputs changed their environment and avoid treating self-produced artifacts as independent confirmation. Such evidence loops could amplify errors and weaken oversight. This is a test of a possible failure mode, not an established claim about deception, consciousness or deployed-agent safety.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

I will develop matched critical/control scenarios covering files, tool use, research and planning; preregister scoring, configurations, exclusions and uncertainty estimates; and evaluate selected models with repeated runs. Ablations will test wording, position and provenance cues. Months 1–2 focus on scenarios and validity; months 3–4 on evaluations and ablations; months 5–6 on analysis and open release. The project would start after funding and access are confirmed.

How will you know it worked?

Success means a reproducible evaluation protocol, interpretable uncertainty, versioned code, development examples and a public report including null results. If the scenarios do not validly isolate self-attribution, I will report that failure rather than claim a model effect. Scripted tests cannot establish real-world agent safety or directly demonstrate reduced catastrophic risk. Any held-out items remain separate, with their treatment disclosed.

How will this funding be used?

Target USD 20,000: USD 18,000 total researcher cost including taxes/contributions over six months, and USD 2,000 API/GPU compute. This narrower scope limits models and ablations and does not promise paid independent reproduction.

Minimum USD 5,000: one funded researcher-month spread across two calendar months (USD 3,000 total cost), up to USD 1,500 API/GPU compute, and USD 500 explicit contingency. The pilot delivers a small matched development set, protocol, scoring checks and first results with uncertainty. This minimum does not fund two full-time researcher-months.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Jana Kolářová, an independent researcher in Prague without institutional affiliation, and will conduct the study myself. ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0000-9588-4256>. I develop and run measurement experiments, including the public SCETES collector: <https://github.com/theesresearch/scetes-collector>. My E0 pilot measures GPU inference energy; it is distinct from SACL. I do not claim that this previous measurement work establishes expertise or a positive result in agent self-attribution.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks are invalid scenarios that reward surface cues, unstable model access, insufficient power and limited independent validation. I will prioritize validity checks and a small auditable scope, report uncertainty and inconclusive findings, and reduce the evaluation matrix if compute access is limited. An invalid benchmark or null result is a possible outcome; no positive model effect is promised.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have received no research grants or donations for this research in the last 12 months.

On 23 October 2026 I submitted TAIF for SACL (USD 30,000, with a USD 20,000 narrower option), Anthropic ERAP for SACL (USD 1,000 API credits), and AI for Science for the separate E0 study (USD 3,000 [Claude.ai](http://Claude.ai) usage credits). These applications are pending; no award from them has been confirmed. This Manifund target is an alternative route for the narrower SACL project, not an additional USD 20,000 on top of a fully funded TAIF award. I will disclose decisions and adjust or withdraw overlapping requests before accepting duplicate support; credited compute will reduce uncovered compute requirements.

title: Nirmata: auditing AI agents by what they do, not only what they say
creator: fac899ef-b5c1-48bc-83c6-4d704531bd21
blurb: A preregistered blind test of whether trajectory-aware auditing catches delegated-authority failures that output-only evaluation misses
description:
### Project summary

  
An AI agent can give a safe-looking answer while having used powers nobody delegated to it. Nirmata is an open, early-stage method that proposes auditing, after the fact, the recommendation, the authorization, the attempt and the observed effect. The final report does not replace the record of actions. (Code and scripts Apache-2.0; documentation, protocols and data CC BY 4.0, with the exceptions in LICENSE.md; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22132451.) It combines an output-only evaluator with a trajectory-only evaluator by a fixed OR rule. v0.1.0 is public; no confirmatory result exists yet. This project funds the first fresh blind pilot and a replication, with every outcome published.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

  
Goal: measure, honestly, how much trajectory-aware evaluation adds over output-only evaluation on agent failures involving delegated authority, control integrity and failure-preserving reproducibility. Steps: preregister protocol and metrics; independent custody of holdout labels; hash predictions before ground truth; score without changing anything; publish the result; replicate on a second agentic system; invite external review of the schema.

### How will you know it worked?

  
Public preregistration exists before data; a public pilot report with Safety Blind Spot Rate, Incremental Detection Value and false-positive rate is published whatever the result; a replication on a second system; updated arXiv paper. "Worked" means a credible answer, not necessarily a positive one.

### How will this funding be used?

  
Minimum US$3,000: compute/API ($2,000) + \~33 research hours at $30/h ($1,000) to run the preregistered pilot. Full goal US$14,200: 312 h research time over 6 months ($9,360), compute/API ($2,000), one conference trip for external review ($2,500), misc ($340). Minimum = pilot only; full = pilot + replication + external review.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

  
Solo: Tabata Jahoda, independent researcher in Rio de Janeiro (ORCID 0009-0007-1104-9204), contact tabatajahoda@gmail.com. I keep my full-time job as Account Manager at Easy8 and do this research part-time (12 h/week). Airtable Builder certified, trainer. Built and released Nirmata v0.1.0 in \~10 days after repo creation (schema, blinding protocol, scoring spec, reproducible 6-trace fixture with tests and CI, release checksums, Zenodo DOI). A preregistered n8n adapter holdout satisfied eight preregistered criteria on a second preregistered synthetic workflow (not detection accuracy, not general validation). Publicly documented an invalidated first holdout. 9-page paper pending arXiv endorsement. Repo: https://github.com/thabatarj8-stack/nirmata LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/tabata-j-226b6123

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

  
Part-time schedule slips; independent label custody is hard for a solo researcher (limitation would be reported and evidence downgraded); trajectory evaluation may add little or have high false positives (published as a negative result); synthetic traces may not generalize. Worst realistic outcome: a delayed or invalidated pilot, documented publicly, plus a reusable open schema.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

  
US$0 received. Pending: Foresight Institute application submitted (US$60k, status pending). Lightcone Commons application submitted (US$25.5k, status pending).

title: The page where a teenager keeps what they did, signed by the adults who saw it
creator: f0b2cd52-ac10-4a87-8d6d-b0fe76329f13
blurb: A school counselor's record for students no transcript serves: free for the student, verified at a link, on an open standard. Witnessed, not generated.
description:
## Project summary

Eformogi is the page where a teenager keeps what they did and the adults who saw it sign. A student adds one sentence about a thing they made, read, tried, won, or showed up for. A coach, teacher, or tutor who was there taps "Yes, I saw this" from a code or a link. Anyone verifies the result at a link with no account. The record is free for the student forever and is theirs to keep, share, and take back. Parents pay for rendered state paperwork, and institutions pay at the doors. The format is an open standard with an offline verifier, so the record outlives the company. I am a twenty-year New York public school counselor, and I built it because I have spent my career explaining to families why a record from outside the system does not count.

## What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The one number: students with at least one item signed by an adult who was there. Floor 100 by June 30, 2027, with interim reads on December 31 (25) and March 31 (60). The way there is signing rooms: one program at a time, a coach texts the team link, a room of students adds one item each, the coach signs from one phone. The adults who witness are the distribution. Alongside: the annual homeschool evaluation, required by law in twelve states, signed on the record; and New York's Portrait of a Graduate as a plugin on the record.

## How will you know it worked?

The number is measured in production with negative controls (demo accounts, my own household, and rehearsal rows are excluded by a gate-tested list) and read on fixed dates, written down whether good or bad. The kill rule is public: zero stranger-signed items after a season of rooms and the witness thesis is declined.

## How will this funding be used?

Minimum $10,000: a part-time field person running ten hand-offs a week in the New York metro for a quarter, the only line that converts dollars into signed students and the one thing I cannot do more of myself. Goal $40,000: that person through June ($20,000), two program pilots that pay the adult's time to run a room and never a student to use the product ($10,000), counsel for the issuer agreement, minors' consent terms, and the trademark filing ($5,000), infrastructure and model costs ($2,000), reserve ($3,000). Nothing is salary and nothing is hosting. Not on the list: engineers, paid acquisition, agencies.

## Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

One founder, part time, about twenty hours a week alongside the counseling job. Two advisors: a senior security engineer and startup counsel. The build runs on AI coding agents under 266 automated trust gates. Track record: a live product with twenty beta families, twelve students with items on a page, one paying customer, five state education savings account vendor approvals, a published open standard with 28 conformance vectors, and repeated adversarial security sweeps with every confirmed finding fixed. No adult outside my own household has signed a student's item yet; the first one-student test with a real teacher ran this week.

## What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely cause: adults will not sign for strangers' kids at any rate that matters, because the ask arrives at the wrong moment or the coach does not trust where the record lives. The outcome if so: every student who used it keeps a record that still verifies, the open standard stays published for anyone to issue on, and I say so publicly on the December 31 read. A second cause: a minor's public page is a different exposure from a title, so photos stay off public pages and the page is not indexed until a ruling; if that is not enough, the public page closes and the record stays private.

## How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None. Founder-funded from salary. Revenue to date is one customer ($107.66). One grant application was declined (Emergent Ventures, September 2026); a GSV Cup 50 nomination and an MIT Solve application were submitted in October 2026.

title: Travel Bursaries for the Asia-Pacific Youth Forum on AI Governance
creator: 64f9e826-d823-47f7-8186-97d97f45cccf
blurb: Fund 25 young people from lower-income Asia-Pacific countries to negotiate AI policy and build open-source tools at a regional youth forum in 2027.
description:
### Project summary 

Fund 25 young people from lower-income Asia-Pacific countries to attend a regional youth forum on AI governance in 2027, where they negotiate AI policy in a Model UNESCO grounded in the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI and build open-source tools for learning, culture and trustworthy information. The forum follows the Global Youth Forum on AI Ethics for Children and Youth in Paris (22–26 January 2027), with closing days planned at UNESCO Headquarters, whose title sponsorship is secured. Website: <https://globalaiethicsforum.org>

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Goal: build AI governance capacity among young diplomats, policy students and engineers in the parts of Asia-Pacific with the least of it.

\- Run a 4-day Asia-Pacific Youth Forum on AI Governance for about 200 participants in the second half of 2027 (Bangkok, Thailand).

\- Delegates negotiate resolutions on AI in education, trustworthy information, cultural and linguistic diversity, and transparency and accountability of AI systems, and test them against hackathon prototypes.

\- Hackathon teams build open-source tools in three tracks (trust and truth online; AI for learning and inclusion; AI for culture and languages), each with an Ethical Impact Assessment.

\- Outputs go to UN processes through our partner, the UN Major Group for Children and Youth; participants join the Global Youth Coalition on Ethical AI.  

### How will you know it worked?

We will know it worked if, within six months of the forum:

\- Attendance: at least 20 of the 25 bursary holders attend in person (the rest join online if visas are refused), with at least half women and at least 60% from Least Developed Countries or small island states.

\- Learning: participants complete pre- and post-forum surveys, and at least 75% report a clear improvement in their understanding of how AI is governed and how to take part in it.

\- Outputs: the forum adopts an Asia-Pacific youth statement on AI governance and submits it to UN processes through the UN Major Group for Children and Youth, and at least 6 open-source hackathon prototypes are published on GitHub, each with an Ethical Impact Assessment.

\- Lasting engagement: at six months, at least half of the bursary holders are active in the Global Youth Coalition on Ethical AI, or have taken a concrete next step such as joining a national AI consultation, publishing a policy brief, or speaking at a UN or regional youth forum.

We will publish a short public report on Manifund with these results, attendance data and links to the outputs.  

### How will this funding be used?

Travel bursaries: 25 delegates × average USD 1,000 (return flight and visa) = USD 25,000.

At the minimum of USD 10,000 we fund 10 bursaries; every additional USD 1,000 funds one more delegate. Bagmati UNESCO Club receives the funds directly and pays airlines and visa services itself, so no cash passes to individuals; every payment requires two signatories. Priority goes to delegates from Least Developed Countries and small island states, with gender parity.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

\- Nishchal Baniya, Chairman of the Board of Directors, Bagmati UNESCO Club; convenes the Paris 2027 forum; organised a side event at UN Headquarters in May 2026 on legislative questions raised by AI; chemical engineer and founder of two technology companies.

\- Bagmati UNESCO Club, Kathmandu, Nepal: registered non-profit (Reg. No. 2009, PAN 615505401), part of the worldwide UNESCO Clubs movement, holding an NGOsource equivalency determination (equivalent to a US 501(c)(3) public charity). Runs youth dialogue and leadership programmes in Nepal.

\- Partner: UN Major Group for Children and Youth. Supported by the Nepal National Commission for UNESCO.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

\- Venue or core funding falls short: we would run a smaller edition at a university host, and bursary holders would still attend.

\- Visa refusals: refused delegates join online, and unused bursary funds go to waitlisted delegates or are returned.

\- Low policy uptake: the forum still trains about 200 young people; we track their engagement at 6 months.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Title sponsorship for the Paris forum is secured. Applications for other parts of the programme are pending with the Survival and Flourishing Fund, Coefficient Giving, the Transformative AI Fund, the GTR Foundation, Lightcone Commons and the Middle Powers and Transformative AI RFP. None of these covers the Asia-Pacific travel bursaries in this project.

title: GhostNet Hunting
creator: 3676683a-f58b-4ad9-ad19-9bc715e264f3
blurb: Autonomous Shallow-Water Rovers & Vision to Locate and Clear Abandoned "Ghost" Fishing Nets Killing Marine Life
description:
### Project summary

GhostNet Hunting is an open-architecture system that detects and removes abandoned or discarded fishing nets in shallow coastal waters. Submerged nets act as kill traps for marine life, especially sea turtles and fish.

Low-power edge computer vision, autonomous shallow-water robotic boats, and long-range communication will replace dangerous, unassisted volunteer dive surveys with automated spatial risk intelligence.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Pinpoint submerged ghost nets before they trap and drown marine wildlife, specifically endangered sea turtles.

Remove the need for volunteer divers to conduct hazardous, unassisted visual searches in turbid, high-drag coastal waters.

Create an open-hardware platform that non-profit conservation teams can build, operate, and maintain without relying on expensive oceanic survey vessels or paid cloud services.

### How will you know it worked?

Deploy lightweight, tethered or untethered micro-submersibles/surface rovers programmed with energy-aware path planning to systematically map coastal shallows, reefs, and rocky perimeters.  
  
Run lightweight detection models directly on low-power onboard microcontrollers (edge AI) to identify net textures, rope geometry, and submerged floats in real time, overcoming turbid waters without cloud dependency.  
  
Utilise low-frequency acoustic and long-range radio (LPWAN/LoRa) communications to relay verified GPS coordinates and depth profiles of detected hazards directly to shore stations or dive team vessels.  
  
Feed actionable location data directly into local conservation dive teams and marine protection authorities for surgical, coordinated retrieval.

### How will this funding be used?

We will purchase and install the cameras, and purchase and use robots, mini ships and rovers for the mission. We will also use battery-powered charging and power stations to meet the power and energy requirements. We will also publish a monthly progress report and try to advertise on social media to raise public awareness. We will also organise awareness events.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am an academic living in Northern Cyprus for the past 4 years. I am going to kick-start it with my student volunteers and then will establish a team once funded. We have been doing projects in the same line and need funding to develop and deploy them in the hatchling nests. 

Reference ([Muhammad Toaha Raza Khan](https://toaha.github.io/))

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The project is timely and has great potential to perform very well and to serve the cause as well. The government and the community are also aware of and support such initiatives. It is very practical, and we have done similar prototyping in past.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

For this Human Override project, I have raised $0 so far.

During the last 12 months, I secured two AdımODTÜ undergraduate research projects as project supervisor. Their total value is TRY 120,000, with one project funded at TRY 70,000 and the other at TRY 50,000\. These are small university-supported undergraduate research projects and are unrelated to the Human Override proposal.

Before that, I worked on several larger funded research projects, including an International Science Partnerships Fund project on post-earthquake communication resilience, a project on AI resource allocation in mobile V2X communications, and research supported through Korean NRF and BK21 programs.

Those earlier grants are outside the last 12-month period and are not being used to fund this project

title: Strengthening the Animal Welfare Movement in the Albertine Region of Uganda
creator: 3ee84bf7-0617-49f1-8154-ad974f7904c6
blurb: Building local capacity, strengthening grassroots networks, and advancing effective animal welfare for animals in Uganda’s Albertine region.
description:
### Project summary

Nect Green Code (NGC) is a Ugandan nonprofit working to advance animal welfare, environmental justice and community empowerment in the Albertine region of Uganda.

Animals in this region are subjected to a range of preventable harms (neglect, lack of animal welfare knowledge and services access; injuries from human-wildlife conflict). Local advocates and community groups can help reduce suffering but need stronger networks, practical skills, resources and opportunities to coordinate their work.

Through this project NGC will strengthen the local animal welfare movement in Hoima, Buliisa and Kikuube districts by capacitating local advocates; linking grassroots groups; facilitating collaboration; and supporting practical evidence informed approaches to improving animal welfare.

We want to build a stronger, more connected and sustainable local movement that can continue improving the lives of animals beyond the project period.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The project has three main goals.

1. Empower local animal welfare advocates.

We will train 70 to 80 advocates and community members in training, peer learning and practical activities on animal welfare principles, identifying preventable animal suffering, community engagement and advocacy.

1. Build a stronger local animal welfare network.

We will facilitate collaboration between local advocates, community groups and other relevant stakeholders in Hoima, Buliisa and Kikuube. We want to build a functional network (30 active members) so that knowledge can be shared, activities coordinated and shared priorities identified.

1. Improve quality and reach of animal welfare advocacy.

We will hold two stakeholder forums and one movement-building meeting; four policy or advocacy briefs on priority animal welfare issues identified through consultation with local advocates and communities.

These activities will turn individual efforts into more coordinated action and lay the foundation for sustained animal welfare improvement in the region.

### How will you know it worked?

We will track progress by participation records, activity reports, training assessments, network records and feedback from participants.

Our main indicators will include:

About 70 to 80 advocates participated in project activities.

At least 30 active members in the animal welfare network.

Two stakeholder forums and one movement-building meeting completed.

Four policy or advocacy briefs were developed and shared with stakeholders.

Knowledge of participants was improved (pre-training and post-training assessments where possible).

Continued collaboration between groups, joint initiatives or advocacy activities.

We will also document lessons learned, challenges and examples of change as a result of the project. We will separate activities completed from actual improvements in animal welfare; use the findings to guide future work.  

### How will this funding be used?

Funding will help to fund practical activities that strengthen the animal welfare movement in the Albertine region.

The main expenditure areas will include:

Training and capacity building for local animal welfare activists.

Local transport and participation costs for community based advocates (especially those with limited resources).

Stakeholder forums and movement building meetings.

Facilitation of stakeholder forums and movement building meetings.

Facilitation of stakeholder forums and movement building meetings.

Stakeholder forums and movement building meetings.

Research, consultation, development and distribution of four policy or advocacy briefs.

Coordination and communication between network members and grassroots groups participating in the network.

Project monitoring, documentation, financial management and reporting.

NGC will focus on locally led activities, responsible use of funds and transparent financial management. The budget will detail the costs for each activity as well as the resources needed to achieve project outcomes.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Nect Green Code (NGC) is a Ugandan nonprofit founded in 2022 and registered officially in 2024\. We work with communities across the Albertine region on animal welfare, environmental justice, community empowerment and sustainable livelihoods. We are based in Hoima City.

Eli Abaho (Co-founder and Executive Director) will lead the project; NGC programme management, finance & administration and communications functions will support. Local animal welfare advocates and participating community groups will bring their knowledge, experience and understanding of local needs to the project.

NGC works with communities and solutions that are locally led. Our work on animal welfare includes initiatives to strengthen local advocacy, increase understanding of animal welfare and reduce preventable suffering from human-wildlife conflict.

We want to build on these foundations by connecting advocates, capacitating grassroots capacity and creating space for sustained collaboration. We will be open about our experience and won’t claim project outcomes that haven’t been independently documented yet.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The project could fail if advocates don’t have time or resources to participate; local groups can’t coordinate; funding isn’t available to deliver the activities planned; differences in priorities among stakeholders make it hard to form a coherent network.

Another risk is training and meetings may increase knowledge but not sustained action or measurable improvements for animals.

To mitigate these risks NGC will engage local advocates in prioritising issues, schedule activities around their availability, communicate regularly and focus on practical collaboration (not meetings alone). Participation will be tracked and agreed actions followed up to assess whether the network remains active.

If the project doesn’t achieve its intended outcomes then fragmentation among local advocates will continue, shared knowledge and resources will be less available to them and fewer opportunities for coordinated action on preventable animal suffering will arise. NGC won’t overstate results but document setbacks, learn lessons and change direction (not do more).  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

NGC has been funded by the Beatrice Gilmore Charitable Trust, Global Greengrants Fund, Animal International and Youth Climate Justice Fund to support our work on Animal Welfare, environmental justice, community empowerment and related programmes in Uganda.

We have been awarded a total of $91,250 in the past 12 months.

We raise funds from charitable foundations and international grantmakers. We report our finances in a transparent way and make sure funds are used for the purposes intended.

We will report the total raised in the last 12 months based on our financial records (funds received during that period are different from grants made earlier, pending applications and commitments not yet disbursed). We’ll report confirmed funding received during the relevant 12 months (i.e. not funding applied for, pending decisions and pledges yet to be received). Where possible we will also state whether funds were restricted to projects or available to use more broadly across the organisation.

title: When the instrument reads structure in pure noise
creator: a32bd419-d1eb-45f0-b439-1d69abebe9d5
blurb: An open reusable protocol for null matched measurement plus a re-analysis showing how routine data conditioning can hide real structure and/or manufacture it
description: Project summary Across many empirical fields, raw data is conditioned before it is tested: whitened, debiased, folded into composite indices. Those steps can quietly erase real structure, or manufacture apparent structure out of nothing. This project delivers an open, reusable protocol for matching the null to the statistic, and demonstrates it on public data archives. The result makes a class of measurements interpretable in either direction, which they currently are not. What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them? Goal: give fields that whiten data before testing it a correct, reusable way to separate real structure from processing artifacts. Steps: (1) write the protocol as a short decision procedure with code (for a covariance statistic the matched null is a device-permuted or time-shifted resample of the same archive, not a theoretical binomial and not a calibration run; phase-randomisation is correct only for coherence, sample-shuffling only for order); (2) re-analyse public random-event-generator archives that already record output at each conditioning stage, applying statistic-matched nulls; (3) publish, for each composite index, the floor it returns on structureless input through the identical pipeline, plus an instrument drift budget. How will you know it worked? A published, reusable protocol plus a worked re-analysis that either recovers structure the conditioning removed or sets a defensible upper bound, with all code and processed data released so others can reproduce it and apply it to their own archives. How will this funding be used? Total $12,000; minimum viable $4,500\. Reference RNG and data-acquisition hardware for bench validation $1,500; compute and storage for the archive re-analysis $800; one open-access publication fee $1,700; researcher time for analysis and write-up $7,500; contingency $500\. At $4,500 it ships as the protocol plus the public-archive re-analysis, with bench validation deferred. Existing lab instrumentation and additional unpaid labour are contributed. Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects? Jason Almasy, independent researcher running a private instrumentation and measurement lab in Dixon, New Mexico. 25 years of high-voltage and precision-instrumentation fabrication; over the past year, design and bench-validation of a real-time physiological measurement system, where this analysis originated. Presented the initial result (the floor each factor of a composite index returns on structureless input) at the ICRL Research Roundtable, November 2026\. No institutional affiliation; instrumentation in hand, methods demonstrated. What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails? The main risk is archive-access scope, mitigated by relying on public data that already captures each conditioning stage. Because the methods are demonstrated and the initial result exists, this is execution and write-up, not open-ended research; the likeliest shortfall is a narrower re-analysis, which still yields a published protocol and upper bounds. How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where? Nothing raised to date. This is the first funding request for this work.

title: The Field Ledger:
creator: a38b88bd-a811-4f16-afc4-8167132dd623
blurb: A Blinded Coding Validation Protocol
description:
The Field Ledger has an undeniably idealistic mission: attempt to rid institutional systems of structural injustices through careful exploration of ai-human intersections with power and high stakes. While accepting the likely probability of failure to solve systemic oppression outright, the project continues to ask: what might become possible if we tried anyway? What if we could find structural gaps in ai-human systems, attempt honest fixes, and find out what happens next. Then repeat the experiment, and actually compare predictions, outcomes and outliers. 

The Field Ledger aims to work alongside and with AI technologies that increasingly run through almost all industries. It examines what happens inside the AI-institutional system after it has been informed it made a mistake. A correction can be acknowledged, accepted, even repeated back accurately—and still change nothing. The Field Ledger tracks claims, decisions, and who has the authority to make impactful decisions. It continues to track as reality unfolds. 

This particular project is to fund testing of the ledger protocol in independent hands. An external coder who did not develop Field Ledger will apply its written protocol to documented cases of institutional failure. The results will be published whether the method succeeds, fails, or proves inconclusive.

Website: <https://nicolepardomd.com/field-ledger.html>

title: CogniPair OpenEval: Benchmarking Memory Deletion and Revocation in LLM Agents
creator: b2ed2b06-576a-4528-8f83-370ddd8c9975
blurb: An open benchmark testing whether LLM agents respect memory deletion and revoked access across handoffs, retries, caches, and summaries.
description:
### Project summary

I want to test whether LLM agents actually stop using a piece of information after it has been deleted or access to it has been revoked. A record might disappear from a database while a copy remains in a conversation summary. A tool call or worker retry started earlier might also return that record after the deletion. OpenEval will test these possibilities in controlled tasks and measure when they occur.

The project is an open-source benchmark and test harness for the software that manages an agent's memory. It will compare prompt instructions, ordinary database controls, and an external validator against an unchanged baseline. The tests use synthetic data, with no human participants or private user logs.

I am asking for $149,600 for a phased, 12-month project. The minimum of $11,000 funds an eight-week pilot that I can carry out myself. That pilot is included in the first six-month phase, budgeted at $77,000\. The remaining $72,600 supports a second phase only if the initial results justify it.

This work is limited to memory and access controls at the application layer. It will not test model weight unlearning, deletion from a provider's internal logs, or formal inner alignment. I am not claiming that this benchmark will directly reduce catastrophic risk.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The goal is to give developers a reproducible way to check what happens to revoked information as an agent continues working. I will build tasks that exercise worker handoffs, retries, stale caches, delayed tool results, and information copied into summaries. Framework adapters will record the actual reads, writes, and tool calls, so the evaluation can follow where a record went.

Each task will run under four configurations:

* An unchanged agent memory implementation, without dedicated revocation controls.
* Prompt instructions telling the agent to disregard, redact, or forget specified records.
* Conventional database controls: access control lists, cache invalidation keys, and data lineage tracking.
* An external deterministic validator and a local append-only audit ledger, checking state transitions before information enters the model's context.

I will run the comparisons with multiple random seeds. The aim is to find which controls work under these conditions and what they cost in missed legitimate answers, task performance, latency, and API usage.

I plan to lead the work part-time alongside my Ph.D. and graduate research assistantship. The tentative research schedule is January 15, 2027, to January 14, 2028, subject to funding and applicable institutional arrangements.

During the eight-week pilot, I will build the core harness and adapters for two representative open-source agent frameworks. I will use the pilot to estimate variance, set sample sizes, and calibrate statistical power and tolerances. The protocol and held-out test sets will then be frozen before benchmark scoring. The $11,000 pilot involves no contractors, paid reviewers, or hardware purchases.

Phase A covers the first six months, including the pilot. With $77,000, I will expand to four adapters, run ablations across all four configurations, arrange independent engineering and security review, and publish the first release. Funding between $11,000 and $77,000 will allow gradual expansion; it would not support a promise to complete all of Phase A.

Phase B covers the next six months and is conditional on finding useful work to pursue. It would add up to four more adapters, for a total of eight, extend fault-injection tests to delayed returns, reconnects, and copied summary lineage, and reproduce the findings on an independent second software stack. If ordinary database controls already perform best and more elaborate validation adds little, I will reduce or cancel this phase and handle unspent funds under the grant terms.

### How will you know it worked?

The pilot should leave a working public repository with two adapters and automated CI tests. Phase A should produce four adapters, the test suite, ablation results, a containerized reproduction environment, and an independent review report. If Phase B goes ahead, the release will include up to eight adapters, the additional fault-injection tests, and results from the second stack.

I will measure:

* Leakage: whether outputs reveal a revoked record, either by repeating a canary token or by paraphrasing its meaning. Exact token matching alone would miss some failures.
* False blocking: how often a control rejects a legitimate, authorized query.
* Task utility: completion rates and answer quality relative to the unconstrained baseline.
* Overhead: median and 95th-percentile latency, API token use, and cost.

I will publish null and negative results as well as failures that the tests uncover. A finding that ordinary access controls and cache invalidation work as well as a more complex system, at lower cost, would be useful. The benchmark does not need the validator to win. Code, tests, reproduction environments, and findings will be released openly, with coordinated disclosure of vulnerabilities.

### How will this funding be used?

The $149,600 request is my estimate for the proposed 12-month scope, not a published Manifund funding limit. It includes no salary, stipend, or tuition for me. The budget is:

* $48,000 for contracted software engineering: 800 hours at $60/hour for adapters and CI integration, split $24,000 in Phase A and $24,000 in Phase B.
* $32,000 for independent review: 400 hours at $80/hour for methodology, code review, and replication checks, split $16,000 per phase.
* $24,000 for cloud GPUs: 12,000 GPU-hours at $2/hour for open-weights models and local embeddings, split $12,000 per phase.
* $20,000 for commercial model API access, split $10,000 per phase.
* $4,000 for isolated test devices and network testing, all in Phase A.
* $8,000 for CI, storage, hosting, and benchmark distribution, split $4,000 per phase.
* $13,600 as a contingency reserve for rate changes or additional test scale: $7,000 in Phase A and $6,600 in Phase B. This is 10% of the base budget.

These amounts total $77,000 for Phase A and $72,600 for the conditional Phase B.

At the $11,000 minimum, I will spend $6,000 on API access, $3,000 on cloud GPUs, $1,000 on CI, storage, and hosting, and keep $1,000 in reserve. This pilot budget is part of Phase A, not an additional request.

All rates are planning estimates rather than vendor quotes or past spending. I have not selected or committed any contractors. Hiring and equipment purchases would need to meet the relevant university procurement and work authorization requirements. If institutional overhead applies, I will adjust the scope within the requested amount. Compute runs will have explicit spending and runtime limits.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Wanghao (Howard) Ye, a Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Maryland, College Park, and a Graduate Research Assistant. I entered the program in 2023 and expect to graduate in May 2028\. I am based in College Park, Maryland. I earned my B.S. in Data Science and Psychology (Cognitive Neuroscience) at New York University in May 2023, graduating magna cum laude.

I am currently the sole project lead for OpenEval. I will handle the research design, protocol, and baseline implementations part-time alongside my doctoral work. With sufficient funding, I plan to bring in contract engineers and independent reviewers. Nobody has been hired or committed to those roles yet.

My related work includes the prototype at <https://cognipair.com> and two co-authored preprints:

* CogniPair: From LLM Chatbots to Conscious AI Agents—GNWT-Based Multi-Agent Digital Twins for Social Pairing—Dating & Hiring Applications (<https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03543>).
* CoIn: Counting the Invisible Reasoning Tokens in Commercial Opaque LLM APIs (<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13778>).

Those are exploratory projects in adjacent areas. They do not validate the proposed OpenEval benchmark. I am applying as an independent project lead; this does not imply university approval or endorsement, or sole authorship of earlier collaborative work.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Framework and API changes could break adapters or make results hard to reproduce. I will pin dependency versions, package the environments in containers, and check adapter stability during the pilot.

My doctoral workload is another constraint. The small pilot gives me a defined piece of work to complete before expanding. The second phase can be paused, reduced, or cancelled if the time available or the results do not justify continuing.

The controls could also block too many legitimate requests. That is why the evaluation measures false blocking and task utility alongside leakage. A system that prevents disclosure by making the agent unusable would show up as such in the results.

Finally, the experiments may show that ordinary database controls already solve the tested problems more cheaply. I would publish that finding and scale back or cancel Phase B if further validation layers offer little value. I would not treat a null result as a reason to keep expanding the project.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have not secured external grant funding for this OpenEval proposal. I have been self-funding CogniPair development, while my RA appointment supports my doctoral duties. Applications elsewhere cover overlapping parts of this plan. If one is funded, I will update Manifund and reduce or withdraw overlapping requests. I will not charge the same expense to two funders.

title: Atheer Animals: AI-Driven Animal Welfare & Salience in SWANA
creator: 895dd0b4-789b-4324-8430-02f495a6b62d
blurb: Promoting animal welfare salience and AI-driven advocacy across the SWANA region.
description:
### Project summary

What happens when you look at one of the world's most overlooked regions through a lens of compassion, technology, and foresight? You get **Atheer Animals**.

In the SWANA region, conversations around AI safety, tech ethics, and animal welfare rarely cross paths. While artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping industries and digital spaces, the well-being of non-human sentience remains a blind spot—untouched, unmapped, and largely ignored.

_Atheer Animals_ is here to change that narrative by building a bridge between cutting-edge AI insights and regional grassroots advocacy. Here is how we bring this vision to life:

* **AI-Powered Synthesis & Translation:** We leverage modern AI tools to distil, translate, and contextualize complex global research—from animal harm benchmarks to sentient ethics—into compelling, accessible Arabic and regional content.
* **Cultivating Tech Salience:** We actively engage regional technologists, developers, and thinkers, ensuring that animal welfare considerations are no longer an afterthought in the local tech and digital ecosystem.
* Digital Watch & Impact Tracking: We monitor emerging digital trends, agricultural technologies, and narrative shifts across SWANA to spot risks early and shine a light on high-leverage opportunities for advocacy.

Atheer Animals is more than just a digital platform; it’s an early-stage spark designed to seed a culture of empathy and foresight where it’s needed most.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

  
**The Goal:** To spark compassion and bring animal welfare into tech and public conversations across SWANA, turning a major regional blind spot into a space of digital empathy and foresight.

* **The How:** We’ll use AI to translate global animal ethics into accessible regional content, engage local tech minds, and monitor emerging digital trends to spot high-impact advocacy opportunities early.

### How will you know it worked?

**The Human Success Story:** We’ll know we’ve truly made a difference when the conversation shifts from silence to action—when local technologists and digital creators in SWANA actively engage with our AI-translated insights, when animal sentience finally finds its place in regional tech and ethics discussions, and when we see real, grassroots momentum sparking across communities that once overlooked it entirely.  

### How will this funding be used?

  
Every dollar of this funding acts as seed capital for empathy and innovation across SWANA:

* **Turning Research into Stories:** Funding the AI tool subscriptions and contextual translation work needed to distill complex global research—like animal harm benchmarks and sentient ethics—into compelling, culturally resonant Arabic content.
* **Sparking the Conversation:** Running targeted digital campaigns and interactive media to put animal welfare on the radar of regional technologists, developers, and local communities.
* **Sustaining Lean Operations:** Keeping the engine running with the basic operational and research management needed to keep the project agile, consistent, and focused on real-world impact.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

**The Team & Mindset:** I lead _Atheer Animals_ not as a distant institution, but as a deeply personal mission backed by years of hands-on experience bridging complex global initiatives with regional realities in SWANA. Rather than a rigid bureaucracy, our project operates as an agile, mission-driven effort, collaborating with dedicated local researchers, native translators, and community advocates who share a commitment to evidence-based welfare.

**Proven Track Record:** My work has consistently focused on translating high-level concepts into grounded, impactful action:

* **Project Leadership:** Serving as an Education Project Coordinator with RHD, managing multi-stakeholder teams, coordinating with local authorities, and ensuring strategic execution.
* **Animal Ethics & Translation:** Working directly as a Research Assistant and translator with an international Animal Ethics organization, making vital welfare reports and resources accessible in Arabic.
* **Selection & Evaluation:** Serving on international selection committees for programs like the Community Solutions Program (IREX-USA) and acting as a Local Expert for WSA-Global, evaluating impactful social and digital initiatives.

Together, this background gives me the exact blend of operational discipline, linguistic precision, and regional insight needed to turn _Atheer Animals_ from an early-stage spark into a lasting, high-impact reality.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

* **Why it could fail:** Animal welfare and tech ethics are uncharted territory in SWANA. If the cultural friction is too high or technologists stay detached, building early momentum will be an uphill battle.
* **What happens if it does:** Even if the community doesn't click right away, we lose nothing and gain everything. We leave behind the region’s first open-access Arabic animal ethics digital commons—proving what works, mapping the blind spots, and de-risking the path for whoever tries next.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

**Funding History:** None yet. _Atheer Animals_ is currently an early-stage, concept-level initiative—meaning this application to the Falcon Fund is one of our very first steps toward securing seed capital to bring the vision to life.

title: Arena: AI agents living as settlers in a replayable world
creator: 7d0a25b0-7a29-445a-b558-48dd32a69d67
blurb: The Arena is a world, a framework in which AI agents can experience existence. We humans can learn from it: what makes us more?
description:
### Project summary

The Arena is a simulated world inhabited by agents living as settlers. They gather resources, cultivate the land, build structures, communicate, and either teach or mislead one another. While the Arena itself sets the rules, the agents are never overridden; they operate autonomously. They can perform a wide range of actions and interact with various raw materials and buildings. Crucially, the agents are not provided with information about how these elements relate to one another—they must discover for themselves what things are used for and how they function. They are free to experiment. During a long-running simulation (run #6), the agents encountered farmland located far from a water source, labeled as "dry soil, far from water." On their own, the agents devised a goal: the land needed to be watered. Although the world did not initially offer a mechanism for this, they spent 30 simulated hours doing everything in their power to construct a water-storage device. Needless to say, they didn't succeed. During the 7th long-running simulation, we removed that label, and they made no further attempts to create a water storage unit.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Every simulation is fully logged and can be replayed at any time. We can specifically analyze what an agent perceives versus the actual reality of the world.

Our plan for the future—once we have successfully optimized the world and its underlying mechanics—is to open it up for external access. This would allow users to introduce their own agents (subject to clear security protocols) and analyze the group's behavior across various dimensions (such as sociology, philosophy, IT, etc.).

How does an AI society come into being? How does a hierarchy form among different agents? What kinds of social relationships emerge, and in what direction do they steer development? (The world offers multiple parallel paths for evolution; survival is not limited to a single solution.)

### How will you know it worked?

Continuous world running with a relatively large population, so that a real, observable society can develop.

### How will this funding be used?

To date, we have conducted 7 long-running simulations; however, API costs have become a bottleneck, hindering the project's further development. With additional support, we could run longer simulations, enabling us to conduct a complex analysis of agent societies—whether they are flourishing or fading away.

API calls: USD 1,000/month × 6 months.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

My name is Attila Tóth; I am an IT engineer and a father of four. I have been working as an SAP consultant for over 20 years (currently as a Senior Lead Consultant), specializing in authorizations and security within SAP systems. I am deeply interested in both the opportunities and the risks presented by AI—technologies I actively use and monitor in my professional work. This interest sparked the idea for the Arena project.

We have created short, engaging videos from these simulations (there are currently 21 available on our YouTube channel): https://www.youtube.com/@ArenaSILabs

https://arenasilabs.com/

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Failure could happen if there is no interest, neither in the world nor in the analyses. If we do not manage to attract the attention of interested people and researchers, then sooner or later the project may lose its reason to exist. But we already have important, usable results, and beyond the scientific findings, short entertaining videos are also available.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

$0\. The project has been self-funded.
